title: The black stone on a cloak
word: The black stone on a cloak
hook: the clans of Mecca nearly come to blows over who will lift the Black Stone, and he lays it on a cloak so every clan lifts together

segments.voice: Yesterday, Khadijah hired him, saw who he was, and asked him to marry her. Your line was she saw him first. Did you thank the one who saw you first? Day eighty-four, the end of week twelve.

Every group project has this moment. The work is almost done, and now there's the part everyone can see, the part that gets the credit, and suddenly everyone wants to do it. In Mecca, around the time the Prophet ﷺ was thirty-five, the Ka'ba had been damaged, and the clans of Quraysh tore it down to its foundations and rebuilt it together, each clan taking a wall. It went well. Until the very last step: setting the Black Stone, the ancient stone in the Ka'ba's corner, back in its place. Every clan wanted the honor. Nobody would back down. Days passed. Swords came out.
screen: `THE KA'BA REBUILT, WALL BY WALL.` → `WHO SETS THE STONE?` → `SWORDS COME OUT.`

segments.voice: Ibn Ishaq tells it. Some clans even dipped their hands in a bowl of blood and swore to fight. Then the oldest man there made a suggestion: let the next man who walks through the gate of the sanctuary decide, and we'll all accept it. They agreed. And the next man through the gate was the young man they called al-Amin. They were relieved. It's the trustworthy one. We accept him. He listened, and then he asked for a cloak. He spread it on the ground and set the Black Stone in the middle of it with his own hands. Then he said: let each clan's leader take hold of a corner. And they lifted it, together, all of them, up to its place. Then he took the stone and set it into the wall. No clan won. Every clan carried. And the man who solved it didn't take the honor for himself; he shared it out. Today Muslims walking around the Ka'ba on pilgrimage kiss the Black Stone, or touch it, or simply raise a hand toward it from the crowd. But it isn't worshiped. A famous report in Sahih al-Bukhari has 'Umar, one of the closest companions, saying to the stone: I know you're only a stone, you can neither harm nor help; if I hadn't seen the Prophet ﷺ kiss you, I wouldn't kiss you. The Qur'an asks believers, in Pickthall's words: “hold fast, all of you together, to the cable of Allah, and do not separate.” And that closes week twelve: a valley of idols, an elephant, an orphan, three homes, a trust, a merchant who saw him first, and a cloak with four corners.
screen: `HANDS IN A BOWL OF BLOOD.` · `THE NEXT MAN THROUGH THE GATE.` · `A CLOAK, AND EVERY CLAN LIFTS.` · `ONLY A STONE, SAYS 'UMAR.` · then, large: `EVERYONE TAKES A CORNER.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: find the solution where everyone carries. Settle, and breathe. Think of one standoff in your life right now. Who does the dishes. Who hosts the holidays. Who gets credit on the team. Picture everyone involved, standing around it. Now look for the cloak: a way for each person to hold a corner, so nobody wins and nobody loses. It doesn't have to be perfect. Just one idea. If you pray, you can ask Allah for a way through. The bell holds the time.
The black stone on a cloak. The clans nearly fight over one honor, and he lays the stone on a cloak so all of them can lift it together.
screen: `THE BLACK STONE ON A CLOAK — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: everyone takes a corner. Today, try your cloak idea in one standoff. Twelve weeks on the path. Tomorrow, he climbs to a cave to be alone. Day eighty-four.

howItsDone: Pilgrims begin each circuit of the Ka'ba at the Black Stone, kissing or touching it if they can reach it, or raising a hand toward it from a distance; Muslims honor it as a stone the Prophet kissed, not as an object of worship.

fork.setup: you've been chosen to settle it. every clan wants the honor of setting the Black Stone, and they're ready to fight. what do you do?
options: set it in place yourself and end the argument.
lay it on a cloak and have every clan lift a corner.
fork.reveal: he spreads a cloak, sets the stone on it, and every clan's leader lifts a corner; then he places it with his own hands.

original.note: Arabic: the Black Stone, set in the eastern corner of the Ka'ba.

trapdoor: what you thought: a holy black rock.
what it means: an ancient stone in the Ka'ba's corner, which he set in place in a way that let every clan share the honor.
what a scholar hears: Quraysh ran short of lawfully earned money for the rebuilding and left part of the old foundation outside the walls, the curved Hijr still seen today (Bukhari).
